newsitem.title: ITALY: Linate to Malpensa transfer logistics under scrutiny.
newsitem.headline: Linate to Malpensa transfer logistics under scrutiny.

text.p: A meeting of key local authority, airline and union representatives was due to take place on Monday in Milan to study the transfer of operations to Malpensa airport from the city's other airport at Linate, air industry sources said.
A two trillion lire ($1.2 billion) capital improvement programme, is underway to consolidate all international and domestic operations at Malpensa.

On completion of the first phase of the project in 1998, SEA will transfer all international and some domestic traffic from Linate. Malpensa will then handle some 80 percent of Milan's passenger traffic and 90 percent of air cargo traffic.
By end-1998 some 2,000 SEA staff are due to move to Malpensa, 46 kms north west of Milan from Linate, which is only 10 kms south of the city.
A further 900 forwarder, transport firm and airline employees are also expected to move to Malpensa.

Cargo operations are seen as an important part of the move and the possibility of financial compensation for cargo agents moving in time for the opening of Malpensa 2000 Cargo City is under consideration by local authorities, the sources said.
The distance between the two airports and the logistical aspects of the move is causing concern amongst cargo agents, they added.

When the first phase is complete in 1998 Malpensa is due to be able to handle some 200,000 tonnes as year of airfreight, rising to 800,000 tonnes by the year 2000. This compares with 126,672 tonnes processed in 1995. passenger capacity will reach 12 million by 1998 against 3.89 million in 1995.
Linate handled 78,790 tonnes and 10.83 million passengers in 1995. -Reuters Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax:5017 ($ = 1621 Italian Lire)
